title: White-portfolio scan for non-attribute cross-boundary routing
objective: Find a recurrent transition boundary where a routing key changes who can perform work, rather than merely enriching an incumbent transaction.
truth_rules: ROUTING KEY VALUE != SEPARATE COMMERCIAL CONTROL PLANE
EXISTING FIELD CAPACITY != OEM-AUTHORIZED PORTABLE CAPABILITY

wide_scan.observed_pressure: Exact model/color/batch repair materials can have low commodity value but high avoided-rework value.
counterevidence: project/development-specific replacement tile is already marketed directly
tile-finding apps advertise rare/discontinued requests, image recognition and idle-tile resale
international surplus-building-material marketplaces already match specific-batch leftovers
wide_scan.verdict: Real identity-key value, but the identity key is already normalizing into specialty-market metadata and search.

wide_scan.observed_pressure: Remote buyers and risk teams repeatedly need physical China site/factory evidence.

evidence.fact: A current QC provider is recruiting a nationwide China freelance-inspector network by geography, travel radius, AQL skill, reporting and response time.
Confirmis repeatedly outsources standardized city-specific site-verification tasks in China.

counterevidence: Confirmis already owns a global site-verifier control plane
Golden Relay sells China site verification and white-label evidence
China business-travel operators offer white-label on-ground support
mature inspection companies and on-demand inspection models already coordinate higher-skill QC
wide_scan.verdict: Generic physical proof and inspection dispatch are already owned/normalizing; low-skill unit economics are weak.

wide_scan.structural_hypothesis: A persistent middle zone exists where an equipment OEM has enough installed base in an ASEAN market to require fast local field service but not enough density to economically internalize a local engineer, service center and parts warehouse.
actors: exporting industrial-equipment OEM with sparse/growing foreign installed base
local multi-brand industrial service company or technician
end customer needing commissioning, maintenance or downtime recovery
OEM remote expert / technical authority / parts owner

evidence.fact: A 2026 advanced-manufacturing globalization white paper says emerging-market demand is shifting from equipment delivery toward turnkey + long-term O&M + local capability building, and cites professional installation/commissioning/O&M shortages in markets such as Indonesia.

Large exporters such as SINOTRUK operate extensive overseas dealer/service/parts networks and recruit dedicated international after-sales roles, showing that dense installed bases can internalize service.
Xi'an Cummins recruits overseas technical support specifically to develop/improve repair capability, supervise service-network performance and parts availability, and resolve overseas service issues.
An industrial machinery manufacturer publicly recruits service/support partners across ASEAN countries.

Nikkiso formed a 2026 strategic service partnership with an established Southeast Asian workshop/field-service network, proving OEM technical authority can combine with third-party local field capacity.
Category-specific multi-brand field service exists in Southeast Asia, including VFD lifecycle service and other multi-brand maintenance models.

claims: RMB 150k-300k comprehensive cost for one overseas engineer deployment/project
5-14 day overseas response versus 24-48 hour customer expectation
overseas after-sales cost 15-25% of contract value versus 5-8% domestically

not_yet_evidenced: persistent installed-base density threshold rather than short transition
repeat service-call density by equipment family
OEM willingness to pay a neutral orchestrator rather than distributor/local partner directly
portable local technician capability after bounded OEM training
training and tooling cost versus expected case flow
wide_scan.next_test: Run causal descent on the installed-base threshold, payer, capability portability, authorization/liability, learning cost, parts boundary, incumbent ownership and normalized economics.

cross_scan_verdict.meta_learning: The strongest fresh boundary is not generic field labor but the possible economic gap between remote-only support and an OEM-owned local service network.

requirements: prove a persistent sparse-installed-base middle zone
identify actual payer and service responsibility
test which equipment capabilities are portable to local multi-brand technicians
determine whether distributor or existing service firm already naturally owns the boundary
do not recruit technicians, contact OEMs, set pricing or build software yet
